title: Tughlaqabad Fort

terrainReference.basis: Original elevation near the south entrance above the modern Mehrauli–Badarpur Road.

mapIdentity.provider: Named OpenStreetMap fortress circuit, gates, defensive walls and separate tomb outwork, compared with published Archaeological Survey of India field descriptions.
mapIdentity.scope: The named 142-point closed mapped city-wall circuit and separate controls for walls, four gate footprints, palace, approach, causeway and fortified tomb. The mapped alignment covers the principal surviving fort precinct and associated southern tomb.

note: Cunningham’s field report records steeply battered stone curtain walls and exposed circular bastions on rocky terrain, with a southern wall about 12.2 m above rock before surviving losses. The 1902 photographs show the uneven ruined wall caps and distinct pale dome, arches and banded stonework of the Tughluq tomb.
